title: Pewaukee clicks down 24% for a second straight week (384 → 292)
detail: Following last week's -29%, /locations/pewaukee fell again from 384 to 292 clicks while position held flat (3.8 → 3.7) — so this is not a ranking loss but a sustained demand or SERP-layout problem. Branded local queries confirm it: 'forage kitchen pewaukee' 411 → 389 and 'forage pewaukee' 30 → 12. Two consecutive weeks of decline warrants action: pull up the Google Business Profile and check for anything stale (hours, a lost 'open' status, dropped photos, a dip in review volume), and compare against Toast in-store sales for 6/20–7/17. If store sales held, this is search-visibility only (possible new competitor in the local pack or a Google map-pack reshuffle); if sales also dipped, it's genuine local demand.

title: 'forage kitchen whitefish bay' lost position 1.3 → 2.0, clicks down 36% (510 → 325)
detail: New this week and a genuine ranking loss on a primary location query — the term slipped out of the #1 slot. The /locations/whitefish-bay page total looks fine (581 vs 584) only because searchers shifted to variants ('forage whitefish bay' +85, 'forage kitchen whitefish bay menu' +18), masking the drop. Someone is now outranking the brand on its own city term. Action: check whether a competitor or an aggregator (Yelp, DoorDash, a Google-hosted result) took the top organic spot, confirm the Google Business Profile is verified and primary, and verify the page title/H1 still leads with 'Forage Kitchen Whitefish Bay'. Recovering the #1 position here is worth ~185 clicks/28d.

title: Champaign branded query recovered to pos 1.1 (+9 clicks) — downgrading last week's alert
detail: Last week's high-priority Champaign flag partially resolves: the lifeblood query 'forage kitchen champaign' sits at position 1.1 with clicks up 83 → 92, and page clicks held steady (266 → 264). The aggregate page position is still depressed (~6.3 vs a 4.0 prior baseline), but that reflects non-branded local terms ('restaurants champaign il'-type queries), not the brand intent that drives orders. Keep the page on watch — if branded clicks stay flat it's fine, but if the non-branded position doesn't recover in 2–3 weeks, refresh the page copy with Champaign neighborhood/landmark keywords and confirm LocalBusiness schema is present.

title: 'Near me' queries slipping for a second week (food near me 10.8 → 11.8, restaurants near me 13.6 → 15.5)
detail: Both high-intent local terms lost ground again this period, continuing last week's trend. 'restaurants near me' (4.1k impr) and 'food near me' (10.4k impr) are big top-of-funnel opportunities that hinge on local-pack signals rather than page copy. Confirm every /locations/* page carries complete LocalBusiness structured data (name, address, geo coordinates, opening hours, telephone, menu URL) and an embedded Google map, and that each location's Google Business Profile category, hours, and photos are current — that's the ranking input Google uses for these unbranded local searches. This has now slipped two weeks running; prioritize the schema audit.

title: Non-branded impressions fell 40k as blog content pulled back — demand/algorithmic, not ranking
detail: Non-branded impressions dropped 238.6k → 198.9k and blog pages lost 15–40% of impressions across the board (kale-vs-spinach -14.6k, forbidden-rice -15.3k, farro-vs-quinoa -6.7k), yet their positions are stable or improved (forbidden-rice 8.3 → 7.8, kale-vs-spinach 6.9 → 7.1). Stable rank + falling impressions = a demand or SERP-feature pullback (seasonal, or AI-overview/featured-snippet cannibalization), not lost rankings. Non-branded is still only ~9.7% of clicks. Rather than chase the decliners, refresh the 2–3 highest-impression posts (forbidden-rice, kale-vs-spinach, fermented-foods): update the publish date, add/refresh FAQ schema to win back snippet space, tighten title tags to the exact query, and add internal links from the homepage and /menu.

title: State Street still the weakest location page (52 clicks, pos 4.2)
detail: Carried forward from last week, unchanged: /locations/state-street-madison-wi draws only 52 clicks vs 161–581 for other locations, despite strong Madison intent ('forage kitchen madison' 909 clicks at pos 1.0) resolving to the homepage. Add prominent homepage links to the State Street and Hilldale location pages so Madison searchers get routed to a specific store, and enrich the State Street page with neighborhood/campus keywords, parking info, and photos. Low urgency but a standing gap.
